name: Robinhood Chain’s own L1 rollup authority

requirements.label: Admin power is not a bare key
A confirmed delay before changes apply, no bypass
Bypass paths of the delay checked and ruled out
Price feed not under one hand
No key shared with another tracked protocol

exit_window: a delay with a bypass, or one not ruled out

narrative.summary: A real, publicly-named 7-of-8 Security Council Safe, plus a Timelock that - corrected in batch 8 - turns out to genuinely gate changes now, just with no separation between who can propose and who can veto.
narrative.detail: Six core L1 contracts on Ethereum mainnet (Rollup, SequencerInbox, CoreProxyAdmin, DelayedInbox, Bridge, Outbox - not the L2 itself) share one authority chain. EXECUTOR_ROLE is held directly by a 7-of-8 Gnosis Safe named by Robinhood’s own governance docs: Robinhood (2 seats), BitGo, Chainlink Labs, Fireblocks, Offchain Labs, Paxos and Talos - though no public source maps a specific address to a specific institution. A second EXECUTOR_ROLE holder is a real, correctly-configured 7-day TimelockController. Batch 8 found and fixed a real bug here: this scorer had a hardcoded note from batch 4 claiming zero PROPOSER_ROLE holders, silently asserted as current fact on every push since - a live replay now shows a real holder (a 6-of-8 Safe), so the timelock does gate something today. But that same Safe also holds CANCELLER_ROLE - whoever can propose a change can also cancel any attempt to veto it, so there’s still no real separation of powers. This group's 14 root signers (7 direct Safe seats + 7 owners of one nested 3-of-7 seat) share none with any other tracked group (crossExposureScore: 100).

cheapest_fix.what: admin power taken away from a bare key

independent_read.why: no code at this address on the chain's mainnet: a derived identifier for a native (non-EVM) entity such as HyperCore, or a contract that lives on another chain (a rollup's own L1 contracts); nothing for this reader to compare here
